basis: Disorder of the synovial bursa, a musculoskeletal structure.
Progressive encephalopathy and generalized lipodystrophy define the syndrome; hepatic steatosis occurs in 30-79%.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; persistent ocular misalignment is reported in 3/8 (~38%). Hypotonia does not establish intrinsic muscle disease.
Deficiency of a plasma factor required for clot retraction is a haemostatic disorder.
Hypertonia, hypokinesia and dyskinesia support a hereditary motor-system disorder; intrinsic muscle or pulmonary damage is not established.
Cutaneous capillary malformations occur in 48/50 patients and define this vascular syndrome; deeper arteriovenous malformations occur in only 16%.
Chronic lymphatic obstruction produces elephantiasis with skin and subcutaneous fibrosis; the lymphatic lesion is not an infection.
IL17RC immunodeficiency causes chronic mucocutaneous Candida infection; esophageal candidiasis occurs in 1/3 (~33%).
Progressive degeneration of cerebellar and other neural pathways; optic neuropathy is reported in 30-79%, supporting direct ocular involvement.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with universal developmental regression; visual loss occurs in 2/5 (40%), with optic atrophy documented in 1/5.
Umbrella for inherited mineral-processing disorders; no additional organ is consistently damaged across the group.
Carcinoma originates in nasopharyngeal epithelium, within the upper airway axis; EBV association does not make the carcinoma an infection.
Inflammation of the facial nerve sensory ganglion; taste loss, hyperacusis and reduced lacrimation reflect neural dysfunction.
Congenital ventricular outflow and septal malformation confined to the heart.
Congenital skeletal myopathy with weakness, atrophy and abnormal muscle histology; respiratory and feeding impairment reflect muscle dysfunction.
Diffuse cerebral cortical malformation causes developmental disability, seizures and motor impairment; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic.
Benign epithelial neoplasm originating in skin.
Hepatic heme-synthesis disorder; motor polyneuropathy and blistering skin erosions are each reported in 30-79%. Abdominal pain alone adds no GI axis.
Callosal hypoplasia, preauricular skin tags and camptodactyly define the syndrome; immune dysfunction occurs in 80-99%. Recurrent pneumonia is a separate infection.
Lysosomal storage disease dominated by neurodegeneration; hearing impairment occurs in 27/73 (~37%). Diarrhea alone does not establish intestinal damage.
Congenital single-ventricle cardiac malformation; pulmonary venous hypertension and pulmonary valve stenosis remain cardiovascular.
Skeletal dysplasia and external auditory canal atresia with conductive hearing loss define the syndrome; both affect all reported patients.
Calculi occupy the kidney or upper urinary tract; mineral composition alone does not establish a systemic metabolic disorder.
Chronic inflammation of the lacrimal gland; the record does not establish a specific infectious or autoimmune mechanism.
Benign papillary neoplasm arising from urinary tract urothelium.
